title: Transactional multi-hunk tagged edits
hypothesis: Giving Sol one atomic tool for multiple non-overlapping tagged replacements in a single file reduces emitted mutation calls, stream-cap pressure, and model latency on multi-location changes while preserving tagged stale-read rejection, syntax safety, focused diffs, and verification behavior.
falsified_if: The treatment loses any deterministic pass, increases failed or stale mutations, permits an overlapping or partially applied edit, causes a whole-file write regression, omits post-edit verification, or fails to reduce mutation calls or latency on the realistic multi-file task without materially worsening the other.
deterministic_outcomes: all public and hidden behavior gates pass
scope and required-file gates pass with no existing-file whole writes
zero increase in failed or stale mutations
every mutating scenario retains successful verification
efficiency_outcomes: stream-cap events and maximum raw tool calls
provider response bytes and prompt/output tokens
decision_rule: Adopt the transactional tool only if every treatment run passes all hard gates with no existing-file whole writes and no increase in failed mutations. On multifile_order_cancellation it must reduce mean mutation calls or elapsed time without worsening the other by more than ten percent. Repeated-text and stale-recovery controls must preserve focused scope, concurrent annotations, stale-read recovery, and verification; otherwise keep the single-range interface as the default.
